lead.headline: Wall Street's production-grade tokenization goes live as DTCC, BlackRock, and JPMorgan clear first trades
lead.tldr: This week marks the shift from tokenization pilots to production rails: DTCC's live trades, Citadel's $400M bet on Crypto.com's securities expansion, and Visa's stablecoin platform for 200M merchants signal that institutional infrastructure is now being priced as a core revenue line, not an experiment.

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, this week institutional infrastructure moved from announcement to live production, and the repricing of who captures value in on-chain finance is already underway.

top_signals.title: Citadel Securities Invests $400M in Crypto.com at $20B Valuation
top_signals.summary: Citadel Securities has invested $400 million into Crypto.com, valuing the exchange at $20 billion. The capital is intended to accelerate Crypto.com's expansion into tokenized securities and traditional financial services.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Citadel's $400M entry at a $20B valuation validates exchange infrastructure as a bridge asset between crypto liquidity and tokenized securities, underwriting the thesis that regulated venues with existing scale will command premium multiples over pure-play DeFi protocols.

top_signals.title: DTCC begins first tokenized stock and Treasury production trades involving JPMorgan, BlackRock and Goldman: WSJ
top_signals.summary: DTCC has commenced the first production trades of tokenized stocks and Treasuries in collaboration with major financial institutions including JPMorgan, BlackRock, and Goldman Sachs. The initiative involves the tokenization of various assets, including Invesco QQQ Trust holdings and SPY shares.
top_signals.why_it_matters: DTCC production trades with JPMorgan, BlackRock, and Goldman represent the critical inflection where tokenized assets clear through existing settlement rails rather than parallel systems, compressing timelines for institutional adoption and marginalizing competing infrastructure plays.

top_signals.title: Exclusive: Visa launches new platform to provide stablecoin services to more than 200 million merchants
top_signals.summary: Visa has launched a new platform enabling banks and fintechs to mint, move, and manage stablecoins. This initiative aims to extend stablecoin services to a network of over 200 million merchants.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Visa's stablecoin platform for 200M merchants effectively deputizes its existing network as the distribution layer for programmable dollars, creating a moat that stablecoin issuers and competing payment networks will struggle to replicate without equivalent merchant density.

top_signals.title: Alpaca raises $135M to fund tokenized agent-first infrastructure6m
top_signals.summary: Alpaca has raised $135 million to develop tokenized infrastructure specifically designed for AI agents. The funding aims to build a foundation that allows autonomous agents to interact with digital assets and blockchain networks efficiently.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Alpaca's $135M for agent-first tokenized infrastructure identifies a specific gap in autonomous economic actor tooling, positioning early for a market where AI agents require native on-chain settlement capabilities rather than human-intermediated workflows.

top_signals.title: BlackRock outlines vision for crypto-TradFi convergence as product pipeline grows
top_signals.summary: BlackRock is advancing its strategy to merge traditional finance with crypto through the tokenization of various assets. The firm plans to expand its product pipeline to include tokenized Treasury funds, iShares ETFs, and private markets.
top_signals.why_it_matters: BlackRock's explicit crypto-TradFi convergence roadmap with tokenized Treasuries, iShares ETFs, and private markets confirms that the world's largest asset manager is underwriting tokenization as a product expansion strategy, not a marketing exercise.

top_signals.title: Japan passes crypto overhaul to bring digital assets under financial rules12m, Japan passes crypto overhaul to bring digital assets under financial rulesJapan’s revised Financial Instruments and Exchange Act introduces crypto insider trading rules, tougher penalties and new oversight requirements for crypto businesses.
top_signals.summary: Japan has passed a comprehensive overhaul of its Financial Instruments and Exchange Act to integrate digital assets into its formal financial regulatory framework. The new laws introduce strict insider trading rules and increased penalties for crypto businesses to enhance market integrity.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Japan's integration of crypto into its Financial Instruments and Exchange Act with insider trading rules and enhanced penalties creates a regulatory template that other G7 jurisdictions will study, raising compliance costs for global operators while potentially accelerating capital formation in regulated Japanese venues.

deals.summary: Alpaca has raised $135 million to develop tokenized infrastructure specifically designed for AI agents. The funding aims to build a foundation that allows autonomous agents to interact with digital assets and blockchain networks efficiently.
Stripe and Advent have reportedly made a $53 billion offer to acquire PayPal. The bid represents a 28% premium over PayPal's recent closing stock price.
Decentralized AI project Nous Research is reportedly in talks to raise at least $75 million. The funding round is led by Robot Ventures and values the company at $1.5 billion.

SBI Holdings has received approval from the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) to acquire a majority stake in the crypto exchange Coinhako. This acquisition is intended to bolster SBI's strategic expansion into stablecoins, on-chain finance, and tokenization.
ORANGE JUICE has raised $40 million to establish a permanent capital firm. The firm intends to acquire businesses while implementing a strategic Bitcoin treasury model.

Miami-based startup Cyclops has raised $20 million in a Series A funding round led by Nava Ventures. The company focuses on enabling payment companies to accelerate settlement processes using stablecoins.

Velocity has raised $38 million to develop stablecoin treasury infrastructure specifically designed for enterprise use. The funding aims to bridge the gap between traditional corporate finance and digital asset management.

Stablecoin startup Velocity has raised $38 million in a Series A funding round led by Dragonfly and FirstMark. The platform focuses on bridging corporate stablecoin usage with traditional banking rails and compliance systems.

on_the_radar.title: Japan passes key bill recognizing crypto as financial product, lowering tax rate
on_the_radar.summary: Japan has passed a key bill that officially recognizes cryptocurrency as a financial product. This legislative change allows for a separate taxation system, significantly lowering the maximum tax rate from 55% to approximately 20%.

on_the_radar.title: US, UK treasuries to align transatlantic rules on tokenization and stablecoins38m, US, UK treasuries to align transatlantic rules on tokenization and stablecoinsThe two governments issued recommendations on the treatment of digital assets as the US prepares to implement a 2025 law on payment stablecoins.
on_the_radar.summary: The US and UK treasuries are working to align regulatory frameworks for tokenization and stablecoins. This coordination comes as the US prepares to implement new laws regarding payment stablecoins in 2025.

on_the_radar.title: UK lays out tokenized finance roadmap with projected £33 billion annual boost
on_the_radar.summary: The UK government has unveiled a strategic roadmap for tokenized finance, aiming to modernize financial infrastructure. The initiative is projected to provide a £33 billion annual boost to the economy by enabling real-time settlement and asset efficiency.

on_the_radar.title: President Trump, White House press Senate to advance the Clarity Act while ethics fight looms
on_the_radar.summary: President Trump and the White House are pressuring the Senate to advance the Clarity Act. This move represents a concerted effort by the administration to establish a formal legal framework for cryptocurrency.

on_the_radar.title: Japan’s largest security token platform moves nearly $3 billion to Avalanche blockchain
on_the_radar.summary: Progmat, the dominant security token platform in Japan, is migrating nearly $3 billion in assets to the Avalanche blockchain. This move represents a significant expansion of real-world asset (RWA) tokenization on a public blockchain.

on_the_radar.title: FTX to distribute $900M to creditors in fifth payment round7m
on_the_radar.summary: FTX is set to distribute approximately $900 million to its creditors as part of its fifth payment round. This move is part of the ongoing bankruptcy proceedings to recover and return assets to affected users.

on_the_radar.title: World Cup final is already the biggest ever prediction market as Kalshi bets top $1.27 billion—with Spain favored to beat Argentina
on_the_radar.summary: Prediction markets are seeing massive adoption with the World Cup final, with Kalshi and Polymarket recording over $29 billion in total trading volume. Kalshi specifically has seen bets exceeding $1.27 billion on the final match.

on_the_radar.title: HSBC Approved for Bank of England Digital Securities Sandbox
on_the_radar.summary: HSBC has become the first applicant approved by the Bank of England to go live in the UK's Digital Securities Sandbox. The bank will utilize its HSBC Orion platform to test the tokenization and settlement of securities.

on_the_radar.title: Ostium Left an Opening for Exploiters and $24m Went Out the Door
on_the_radar.summary: The synthetic trading platform Ostium suffered a security exploit resulting in the loss of approximately $23.75 million. The stolen funds were primarily in the form of USDC stablecoins.

on_the_radar.title: Injective Files SEC Transfer Agent Application for Onchain Securities
on_the_radar.summary: Injective has filed a transfer agent registration with the SEC to enable onchain securities ownership records. This move aims to integrate traditional Wall Street market infrastructure with blockchain technology.

on_the_radar.title: 'We're going to get it done': Crypto bill faces what could be final test over Trump conflicts of interest
on_the_radar.summary: There is growing optimism regarding the passage of a comprehensive crypto bill in the U.S. However, the final timeline may be affected by discussions surrounding potential conflicts of interest involving Donald Trump.

on_the_radar.title: Morgan Stanley’s E*TRADE Launches Spot Crypto Trading
on_the_radar.summary: Morgan Stanley's E*TRADE platform has officially launched spot cryptocurrency trading for eligible clients. The service provides access to Bitcoin, Ether, and Solana via a partnership with Zero Hash.

TradFi doesn’t want DeFi. It wants blockchain.

linkedin_post:
DTCC cleared its first production tokenized trades this week. Not a pilot. Production. JPMorgan, BlackRock, Goldman. QQQ. SPY. The assets everyone already owns, now moving on-chain through existing settlement rails.

This is the repricing event we've been tracking. For three years, tokenization was priced as R&D. A line item in innovation budgets. Now it's clearing through the same infrastructure that handles $2 quadrillion in annual volume. The question is no longer whether institutions adopt on-chain settlement. It's who captures the economics.

Citadel's $400M into Crypto.com at $20B says regulated venues with existing liquidity and compliance stacks will command premium multiples. Visa's stablecoin platform for 200M merchants says distribution, not issuance, may be the scarcer asset. BlackRock's product pipeline—tokenized Treasuries, iShares, private markets—says the world's largest asset manager is underwriting this as core revenue, not a side experiment.

We underwrote stablecoin infrastructure and tokenized securities as separate sectors. They're converging faster than our models assumed. The specific thing that would kill our current thesis: DTCC volume stalls or major issuers retreat to parallel private chains, proving the production launch was regulatory theater rather than structural shift. We're watching Q3 DTCC disclosures for that read.

Alpaca's $135M for agent-first infrastructure is the outlier that sharpens the picture. Autonomous economic actors don't need human-intermediated settlement. They need native rails. The infrastructure being built for today's institutions will serve tomorrow's agents. Same pipes, different users.

The value shift is from protocol tokens to regulated infrastructure equity. We are repricing accordingly.
